steps.tx: Target-organ end-organ unresponsiveness to circulating parathyroid hormone produces a biochemical state of hypocalcaemia with paradoxically elevated hormone levels. Termed **pseudohypoparathyroidism**, this heterogeneous group of genetic disorders stems from defects in the parathyroid hormone receptor-adenylate cyclase signaling cascade. In the classic form, pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1a, loss-of-function mutations in the GNAS1 gene impair the stimulatory alpha-subunit of the G-protein (Gs-alpha). Because maternal GNAS1 expression is imprinted in the renal proximal tubule, maternal inheritance causes severe renal PTH resistance, hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, and blunted urinary cyclic AMP generation.

left.title: Primary Hypoparathyroidism
points: Serum calcium low with high serum phosphate
Intact PTH is undetectable or inappropriately low
Normal receptor responsiveness to exogenous PTH

right.title: Pseudohypoparathyroidism (PHP-1a)
points: End-organ resistance to PTH at receptor level
Serum calcium low with high serum phosphate
Intact PTH is markedly elevated (> 100 pg/mL)
Blunted urinary cAMP response to exogenous PTH

steps.tx: A constellation of distinctive somatic and skeletal dysmorphic features characterizes individuals inheriting maternal GNAS1 inactivating mutations. Classically designated as **albright hereditary osteodystrophy** (AHO), the physical phenotype comprises short stature, rounded facies, short neck, obesity, and subcutaneous ossifications. The hallmark skeletal abnormality is brachydactyly, characterized by shortening of the fourth and fifth metacarpals and metatarsals, producing dimples over knuckles when fists are clenched (Archibald sign). In addition to PTH resistance, patients frequently exhibit multi-hormone resistance to thyroid-stimulating hormone, gonadotropins, and growth hormone-releasing hormone.

steps.tx: Genomic imprinting of the GNAS locus dictates distinct biochemical and phenotypic outcomes based on parental origin of transmission. When mutated GNAS1 is inherited from the father, maternal tissue expression of Gs-alpha remains intact in the renal proximal tubules. Consequently, affected offspring develop the physical phenotype of Albright hereditary osteodystrophy without biochemical endocrine resistance, a condition designated **pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism** (PPHP). Patients exhibit classic brachydactyly and short stature, but maintain completely normal serum calcium, phosphate, and intact parathyroid hormone levels, requiring clinical recognition to guide familial genetic counselling.

steps.tx: Latent neuromuscular hyperexcitability induced by low ionized calcium can be rapidly elicited at the bedside. Tapping the facial nerve trunk anterior to the external auditory meatus elicits the **chvostek sign**. In hypocalcaemic individuals, mechanical stimulation induces ipsilateral contraction of facial muscles, ranging from twitching of the oral commissure to spasm of the entire facial hemiface. Although positive in over eighty percent of hypocalcaemic patients, it is non-specific, occurring in roughly ten percent of healthy euthyroid individuals with normal calcium.

steps.tx: Ischaemic provocation of peripheral nerve trunks unmasks latent motor axon irritability with exceptional clinical specificity. Inflating a blood pressure cuff on the upper arm twenty millimetres above systolic pressure for three minutes elicits the **trousseau sign**. Local ischaemia and hypocalcaemia provoke tetanic contraction of hand muscles, producing the classic obstetrician hand posture with thumb adduction, metacarpophalangeal flexion, and interphalangeal extension. Exhibiting over ninety-four percent sensitivity and near-perfect specificity, it represents a superior clinical indicator of acute tetany.

steps.tx: Extracellular calcium concentrations dictate neuronal and myocardial action potential thresholds by modulating voltage-gated sodium channel activation. When extracellular calcium falls, the membrane potential required to open sodium channels shifts closer to the resting potential, causing **neuromuscular irritability**. Nerves depolarize spontaneously with minimal stimuli, producing distal paresthesias, muscle cramping, and bronchospasm. On electrocardiography, hypocalcaemia prolongs the ST segment and delays repolarization, causing marked prolongation of the corrected QT interval and predisposing to torsades de pointes ventricular tachyarrhythmias.

steps.tx: Distinguishing the various subtypes of pseudohypoparathyroidism requires dynamic functional testing of renal cyclic adenosine monophosphate generation. Infusing synthetic parathyroid hormone (Ellsworth-Howard test) measures urinary cyclic AMP and phosphate excretion. In healthy subjects and primary hypoparathyroidism, PTH infusion stimulates a tenfold surge in urinary cyclic AMP. In **pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1**, cyclic AMP production fails to rise due to defective receptor coupling. In type 2, cyclic AMP rises normally but phosphaturia fails, demonstrating a downstream signaling defect.
steps.say: Distinguishing the various subtypes of pseudohypoparathyroidism requires dynamic functional testing of renal cyclic adenosine monophosphate generation. Infusing synthetic parathyroid hormone in the Ellsworth-Howard test measures urinary cyclic AMP and phosphate. In primary hypoparathyroidism, PTH infusion stimulates a marked surge in urinary cyclic AMP. In pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1, cyclic AMP fails to rise. In pseudohypoparathyroidism type 2, cyclic AMP rises normally but phosphaturia fails, demonstrating a downstream signaling defect.

steps.tx: Therapeutic protocols for pseudohypoparathyroidism mirror those of primary hypoparathyroidism, focusing on active vitamin D and mineral repletion. Administering oral active **vitamin d** analogues such as calcitriol bypasses the renal one-alpha-hydroxylase defect, stimulating intestinal enterocyte calcium absorption and suppressing compensatory parathyroid hyperplasia. Co-administered oral calcium supplements restore normal ionized calcium concentrations, eradicating neuromuscular tetany and preventing secondary tertiary hyperparathyroidism. In individuals with Albright osteodystrophy, clinicians must maintain routine screening for subclinical hypothyroidism and growth hormone deficiency to optimize growth.
